column3: Exactly what to do (with example, tied to Cairo's next target)

Whenever he shows pain or discomfort, model 'it hurts' or 'hurts here' and help him point to the spot (he already labels body parts). Example: he's upset and holding his mouth - say 'hurts? mouth hurts?' and touch his mouth; reward any attempt to say or point. Add a 'hurt' button on his AAC.

column2: Name a feeling in the moment
column3: Name his emotion as it happens so the word attaches to the real feeling. Example: he's frustrated - 'you're mad'; delighted - 'you're happy'; tired - 'you're tired'. No demand to repeat; just model. Aim to catch 2-3 feeling moments a day.

Stretch his 3-word 'I want ___' toward 4 words. Example: he says 'I want chips' - model 'I want eat chips' as you give it; at drink time 'I want drink water'. Use the pause-and-wait first so he tries the longer form himself.

Hold a wanted item, wait 3-5 sec with an expectant look so he initiates/extends before you give it. Example: he reaches for iPad - you wait - he says 'iPad' - wait again - 'I want iPad' - then hand it over.

column2: Honour the attempt, model back fuller
column3: Always give the item when he communicates, then repeat it clearer/longer. Example: he says 'ipad' meaning it - give it and say 'iPad - I want iPad'. Never withhold because the word wasn't perfect (that's the apraxia, not refusal).
Beyond want/refuse, practise yes/no about facts. Example: 'Your name is Ahmed? ... No - my name is Yusuf'; 'Is this a cat?' (show a dog) - help him say 'no'. Keep it light and playful.
Short imitation practice on his current sounds (R, Sh, j) and 2-word combos. Example: 'red car', 'big dog', 'more juice'. Keep words from things he wants so it's motivating. Honour approximations.
Prompt him to START greetings, not just respond. Example: when someone arrives, cue him to say 'hi' or 'how are you?' first; wave and model if needed. Target initiating with family members.
Help him ASK, not just answer. Example: coach him to ask 'what's your name?' or 'how old are you?' to a family member, then they answer warmly. Turn it into a back-and-forth game.

column2: Describe a simple picture (new Cairo program)
column3: Show a single-event picture and ask 'what do you see?' Model a short sentence. Example: picture of a boy eating - 'boy eating apple'. Use varied pictures so he describes, not memorizes.

Model on his device in real moments - press the button as you say the word. Example: at snack press 'eat'; for iPad press 'iPad'; add and use a 'hurt' and a few feelings buttons. Accept speech OR button as success.
He knows red/orange/green/blue - add one new colour (yellow, then pink). Example: sort toys, 'give me the YELLOW one'; name colours of his food.
He counts to 15 and knows value 1-3; push value to 5. Example: 'give me THREE chips' then count them; put the right number of blocks on a number card.
He knows all letters and sounds A-O. Example: 'what sound does M make?'; find a letter on a sign; match a letter to a word that starts with it.
He knows square/triangle - add rectangle, oval. Example: find shapes around the house; match shape to shadow.
He follows two steps - try three as he succeeds. Example: 'get your shoes, bring them to me, and sit down'. Help only if needed.
Trace lines, zigzags, staying on the dots with less impulsivity. Example: thick marker, 'follow the road' dotted lines; praise staying on the line.

column2: Number copying 1-5, fade the help (Cairo target)
column3: Trace then copy numbers 1-5, reducing hand-help over time. Example: today guide '3' lightly; next time just start the stroke; aim for independent.
He waits 15 sec without behaviour - stretch toward 30. Example: 'wait' with a visual or count before giving something he wants; extend the count slowly.
Back-and-forth play that builds waiting and shared attention. Example: roll a ball 'my turn... your turn'; stack blocks one each.

column2: End on a success + catch him being good
column3: Finish each mini-session with an easy win and praise/reward his tries and waits. Example: end counting with one he nails - 'great counting!' + a chip or iPad turn.

Watch with him, pause when it pauses, model the word, cheer attempts. Example: Ms Rachel - when she waits for a word, you say it and wait for him to try. A few engaged minutes beat a long passive stretch.
